Hi Amanda / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed set of next steps so your engineers can start experimenting with Redwood locally: 

Key takeaways from the call:
- You plan to prototype on TypeScript (Node) first, with a Python microservice for preprocessing later.
- Target environment: staging on our hosted API, then move to a VPC Private deployment for production.
- Primary use case: reranking + embeddings for semantic search, with structured output for tool-calling to fetch user records.
- Security: SSO and Org-managed keys; your infra team will evaluate mTLS and KMS integration.

Immediate asks / next actions:
1) SDK quickstart and environment checklist (attached). The PDF has both Python and TypeScript steps; starter sample app zip attached.
2) Please confirm which auth path you want us to demo this week — API key (fastest) vs mTLS (preferred for VPC).
3) Marcus / Vivek to run a 45-min tech deep-dive: SDK install, auth, routing policies, and embedding/reranker config.
4) We’ll share a small mutual action plan (MAP) for timelines / deliverables.

Attachments included: redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf (quickstart, env vars, common pitfalls), starter-sample-app.zip (TS + Py samples), MAP_StellarFleet_Redwood.xlsx

Proposed times for the technical deep-dive:

Hi all — quick technical notes and snippets so Tom’s team can start configuring the staging environment before our call. I’ll run the demo against your staging API key.

Auth options (priority):
- API Key (short-lived): simplest. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var locally/staging.
- mTLS + Mutual Auth: supported for Private deployments. Requires cert distribution; our docs include an nginx example and Vault integration.
- KMS/HSM: we support AWS KMS envelope encryption for customer-managed keys during Private deployments.

Minimal env vars (TypeScript quickstart):
- REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-staging-xxxx
- REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://api.redwood.ai
- REDWOOD_MODEL=redwood-gptx-1.0
- REDWOOD_EMBEDDING_MODEL=redwood-embed-1.0
- REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS=120000

TS SDK install + sample run (from starter-sample-app):
1) npm install @redwoodai/sdk axios
2) // .env (use dotenv in dev)
   REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-staging-xxxx
   REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://api.redwood.ai
3) node ./samples/ts/embedding_rerank_demo.js

Example pseudo-code (TS) for embeddings -> reranker -> tool call:
const rdw = require('@redwoodai/sdk');
const client = rdw.client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_BASE_URL });

// 1) create embeddings for query
const embeddings = await client.embeddings.create({ model: process.env.REDWOOD_EMBEDDING_MODEL, input: query });
// 2) search Pinecone (your code) to get candidates
// 3) call reranker to score candidates
const rerank = await client.rerank.score({ model: 'redwood-reranker-1.0', queryEmbedding: embeddings.data[0].embedding, candidates: candidateDocs });
// 4) structured output -> tool call
const structured = await client.chat.create({ model: process.env.REDWOOD_MODEL, messages: [{ role: 'system', content: 'Return JSON with fields: id, action, params' }, { role: 'user', content: 'Enrich this candidate' }], functions: [{ name: 'enrich', parameters: { type: 'object' } }] });
// parse structured.output and call your enrichment API with selected ids

Local testing tips:
- Use the included mock server (samples/mock_enrichment) to simulate your enrichment endpoint.
- Use the --dry-run flag in sample app to avoid hitting production tokens accidentally.
- For latency testing, enable per-route tracing in Redwood Console and share traces with us prior to the call.

Attachments: starter-sample-app.zip contains samples/ts/embedding_rerank_demo.js, samples/py/preprocess_local.py, Dockerfile for local run.

If you can share a short-lived staging key before 09:30 PT I’ll pre-load a demo dataset and validate the end-to-end flow.

Thanks —
